qs.q: Which condition is classified as a vascular defect causing bleeding disorders?
qs.e: Vitamin C deficiency is a classic vascular defect leading to bleeding disorders. ITP is a platelet disorder, and Hemophilia A is a congenital factor deficiency.

qs.q: The most common inherited bleeding disorder is ---
qs.e: Von Willebrand disease is the most common inherited bleeding disorder.
vWD affects ~1% of the population — the most common inherited bleeding disorder worldwide.

ai.subject: Pathology
ai.summary: Bleeding disorders are conditions where normal hemostasis fails, leading to excessive or prolonged bleeding. They arise from platelet defects, coagulation factor deficiencies, or vascular abnormalities. Clinicians must identify the underlying cause to guide targeted therapy.

sections.p: Bleeding disorders are characterized by spontaneous or trauma‑induced bleeding that is disproportionate to the injury. Diagnosis requires a clinical history, physical exam, and a focused laboratory workup to locate the defect.

faq.q: What is the most common inherited bleeding disorder?
faq.a: Von Willebrand disease, caused by deficient or defective vWF leading to impaired platelet adhesion and low factor VIII.

faq.q: How do I differentiate hemophilia from von Willebrand disease?
faq.a: Hemophilia shows isolated prolonged aPTT with normal vWF; von Willebrand disease shows prolonged bleeding time, prolonged aPTT, and low vWF antigen/activity.
